extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent applicants/agents (patent prosecution practitioners)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for examination and entry (or denial) of amendments and supplemental replies during patent prosecution, including preliminary amendments, bona fide but non-responsive replies, second/subsequent replies, and amendments after final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment_of_non-compliant_amendments_37_CFR_1.121
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment submitted after March 1, 2001 fails to comply with 37 CFR 1.121, the Office will notify applicant by a Notice of Non-Compliant Amendment and give applicant a period to comply. Preliminary amendments receive a 30-day/one-month time limit for reply with no extensions; amendments after a non-final Office action receive a 30-day/one-month time limit with extensions permitted under 37 CFR 1.136(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to submit a timely reply will result in examination without entry of the preliminary amendment or abandonment if for non-final amendments that allow extensions. See MPEP § 714.22 for non-compliant amendments after final rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bona_fide_amendment_vs_serious_deficiency
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment that substantially responds to a non-final Office action and is a bona fide attempt to advance prosecution but contains a minor deficiency may be acted on; serious deficiencies (unsigned, not filed in reply) require different treatment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If minor (e.g., fails to treat every rejection), examiner may act and issue new Office action possibly reiterating unaddressed matters. If serious omission, examiner should either (A) if sufficient time remains, notify applicant that omission must be supplied within remaining reply period, or (B) if insufficient time, set an extension under 37 CFR 1.135(c). Examiner should not further examine on merits until omission is timely supplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: New_time_period_under_37_CFR_1.135(c)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) authorizes giving a new time period (one month/30 days) for applicant to complete a reply when an amendment is a bona fide reply but contains an inadvertent omission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicant must supply the omission within the new time period (or any extensions under 1.136(a)) to avoid abandonment; applicant may file a continuing application or further reply as permitted under 1.111. Examiner is not required to grant but may do so; telephone notification preferred and must be summarized in an interview record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inadvertent_vs_deliberate_omission
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) applies only when the missing matter or lack of compliance is considered 'inadvertently omitted.' Deliberate omission (e.g., refusing to elect a species believed improper) is not covered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once inadvertence is brought to applicant's attention, inadvertence no longer exists and a second Office action giving another 1-month time period under 1.135(c) would not be appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner_discretion_to_deny_37_CFR_1.135(c)_relief
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.135(c) authorizes but does not require granting an additional time period; examiner may refuse if applicant is attempting to abuse the practice or if there is sufficient time remaining to file a reply within the existing reply period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If examiner declines, they should notify applicant by telephone or Office communication that the reply must be completed within existing reply period (or extensions under 1.136(a)) to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telephone_notification_and_interview_recording
rubrics_metrics.description: When notifying applicant that an omission must be supplied within the remaining time for reply, telephone notification is preferred when possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If notified by telephone, an interview summary record (see MPEP § 713.04) must be completed and entered in the file to provide a record. If telephone not possible, notify in an Office communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-application_of_1.135(c)_after_final
rubrics_metrics.description: The practice under 37 CFR 1.135(c) of giving a time period to supply an omission does not apply after a final Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments after final are approved for entry only if they place the application in condition for allowance or in better form for appeal; otherwise denied entry. Applicant may obtain additional time under 1.136(a) to file supplemental amendments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner_options_when_reply_after_final_substantially_places_in_condition_for_allowance
rubrics_metrics.description: When a reply to a final action substantially places the application in condition for allowance, examiner may request applicant authorize an examiner's amendment to correct omission, in which case date of reply is date of authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner may also enter the reply, withdraw finality, and issue a new Office action (non-final, final if appropriate, or close prosecution on merits under Ex parte Quayle). These are at examiner's discretion; applicant remains responsible to provide complete reply under 37 CFR 1.113.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form_paragraphs_for_bona_fide_non-responsive_replies
rubrics_metrics.description: Form paragraph 7.95 (and optionally 7.95.01) should be used where a bona fide reply is not fully responsive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form 7.95 sets a 1-month/30-day period (whichever longer) for applicant to supply omitted matter; extensions may be granted under 37 CFR 1.136(a). Examiner note reiterates inapplicability where omission is deliberate or after final action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack_of_arguments_in_response_guidance_7.95.01
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants should submit argument under 'Remarks' pointing out disagreements and must discuss references applied against claims explaining how the claims avoid or distinguish them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form paragraph 7.95.01 is intended primarily for pro se applications and must be preceded by form paragraph 7.95.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preliminary_amendment_entry_rules_37_CFR_1.115
rubrics_metrics.description: Preliminary amendments (received on or before mail date of first Office action) will be entered unless disapproved by the Commissioner. They may be disapproved if they unduly interfere with preparation of the first Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Factors for disapproval include the state of preparation of the first Office action as of receipt and the nature of changes to specification/claims that would result from entry. Certain filing timing (e.g., within 3 months of filing date, national stage entry, CPA filing date, or last day of suspension requested under 1.103) protects entry and these periods are not extendable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second_or_subsequent_supplemental_reply_entry_rules_37_CFR_1.111
rubrics_metrics.description: A second (or subsequent) supplemental reply will be entered unless disapproved; it may be disapproved if it unduly interferes with an Office action being prepared in response to the previous reply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider state of preparation of the responsive Office action and nature of changes to specification/claims that entry would cause. Applicants encouraged to include complete reply in first reply to avoid supplemental replies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors_for_denying_entry_undue_interference
rubrics_metrics.description: Two conditions for denying entry of preliminary or second/subsequent supplemental replies: (A) examiner has devoted significant time preparing an Office action before receipt; and (B) entry would require significant additional time to prepare the Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once conditions met, examiner should obtain SPE approval before denying entry. The rule applies to both preliminary amendments under 1.115 and supplemental replies under 1.111.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examples_of_changes_justifying_denial_of_entry
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry may be denied if the amendment/reply: (A) amends the claims; (B) adds numerous new claims; (C) amends the specification to change scope of claims; (D) amends spec raising new matter; (E) includes arguments; (F) includes affidavit/declaration under 37 CFR 1.131/1.132; or (G) includes evidence traversing prior rejections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This list is not exhaustive; any situation meeting the two-condition test may support denial. Obtain SPE approval before denying.

rubrics_metrics.name: When_disapproval_is_inappropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: Denying entry is inappropriate if either (A) the examiner has NOT devoted significant time to prepare an Office action prior to receipt, or (B) entry would NOT require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thus, the amendment/reply will be entered unless denied for other legitimate reasons (see MPEP § 714.19).

rubrics_metrics.name: Situations_where_entry_should_still_be_allowed_despite_prior_exertion
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if examiner devoted significant time, disapproval is inappropriate if the amendment/reply: (A) merely cancels some pending claims; (B) amends claims to overcome 35 U.S.C. 112, second paragraph; (C) amends claims to place application in condition for allowance; or (D) only includes examiner-suggested changes and would not require significant additional time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry should be made in these situations; supplemental replies nonresponsive to mailed Office actions will not prompt a new Office action but applicant may be notified as a courtesy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Immediate_inspection_checklist_for_amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: All amended applications forwarded to the examiner should be inspected immediately to determine: (A) proper signature; (B) filing within statutory/shortened period or time limit; (C) full responsiveness and compliance with 37 CFR 1.121; (D) whether changes warrant transfer; (E) whether application is special; (F) if claims suggested for interference copied; (G) traversal of restriction requirement; (H) use of non-permanent 'easily erasable' paper; (I) applicant-cited references; (J) terminal disclaimer filed; (K) addition of matter involving security.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate inspection prevents abandonment and allows timely notification of deficiencies if sufficient time remains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling_actions_when_office_action_crosses_in_mail_with_amendment
rubrics_metrics.description: When a supplemental action is necessary because an amendment filed on or before the mailing date of the regular action reaches the Technology Center later, prepare a supplemental action headed 'Responsive to amendment of (date) and supplemental to the action mailed (date)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplemental action should specify which portions of prior action are to be disregarded and point out that the period for reply runs from mailing of the supplemental action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-permanent_paper_and_permanent_ink_requirement_37_CFR_1.52(a)
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.52(a) requires 'permanent dark ink or its equivalent' on papers which become part of the record. 'Easily erasable' paper violates this requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If non-permanence discovered early, applicant is promptly notified and required to file a permanent copy within 1 month or order the PTO to make a copy at applicant expense. If discovered later, require permanent copy but do not hold up action; physical entry will be from the permanent copy. Photocopies or facsimile on satisfactory paper acceptable; original signatures must be applied after copy if required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Telegraphic_amendment_not_entered
rubrics_metrics.description: When a telegraphic amendment (telegram) is received, the telegram is placed in the file but not entered and applicant is notified that the telegram is not accepted as a reply to the previous Office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Time period for reply continues to run and is extendable under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excess_claims_payment_of_additional_fee
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims added in excess of the filing fee may be presented on payment of an additional fee (see MPEP § 607); these excess claims may be presented any time after the application is filed, including before the first action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure correct additional fee procedures per MPEP § 607.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments_after_final_requirements_37_CFR_1.116
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments after final action must comply with 1.114 or 1.116. After final rejection or action, amendments may be made to cancel claims or comply with prior requirements of form, or to present rejected claims in better form for appeal. Amendments touching merits after final may be admitted upon showing good and sufficient reasons why they are necessary and were not earlier presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No amendment as a matter of right in appealed cases; after decision on appeal, amendments only as provided in §§ 1.198/1.981 or to carry into effect recommendations. Admission or refusal to admit amendments after final does not relieve application from appeal/abandonment conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-final_interview_policy
rubrics_metrics.description: One personal interview by applicant may be entertained after final action if circumstances warrant; ordinarily only one request should be granted, though in exceptional circumstances examiner may initiate a second if it would materially assist allowance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage applicants to include a range of claim alternatives (broad to detailed) by time of filing or at least by first reply to alleviate post-final difficulties.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final_rejection_time_for_reply_and_advisory_action_procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant replies within 2 months to a final rejection setting a 3-month shortened statutory period and the Office does not mail an advisory action until after the 3-month period, the period for reply for extension-fee calculation will be the date the advisory action is mailed but never later than six months from the final rejection date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners must include specific shortened-statute wording in final rejections (language provided in MPEP). If first reply not filed within 2 months, extension fees are calculated from end of reply period set in final rejection. Failure to file within shortened period results in abandonment unless extended under 37 CFR 1.136.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry_not_a_matter_of_right_after_final
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant cannot as a matter of right amend finally rejected claims, add new claims after a final rejection (except under 37 CFR 1.116), or reinstate previously canceled claims; compliance with showing under 1.116(c) is expected for amendments after final.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A reply under 37 CFR 1.113 to a final rejection is limited to (A) amendment complying with 1.116; (B) Notice of Appeal (and fee); or other limited actions. Failure to properly reply under 1.113 results in abandonment.
